items.title: Stock Radar: Leela Palace stock hits fresh record highs in August 2026; time to buy or book profits?
items.description: Leela Palace Hotels stock broke a bullish pattern, suggesting higher prices ahead. Experts recommend buying the stock for a target of Rs 570. The stock has shown improvement in its price structure and uptrend. Traders can consider a stop loss at Rs 495 for risk management.

items.title: Supreme Court rulings set to raise insurers' third-party liability
items.description: General insurers face higher motor third-party claim reserves due to Supreme Court rulings. A recent ruling fixes homemakers' notional income, increasing claim payouts. This interpretation is expected to raise claim outgo significantly over eighteen months. Insurers also face policy standardization for occupant and pillion-rider coverage. Motor third-party insurance remains challenging with rising claim costs and slow premium growth.

items.title: MSCI Rejig: Adani Energy Solutions, Lenskart Solutions make the cut; SBI Cards, Astral to be excluded
items.description: Astral Ltd., Balkrishna Industries Ltd. and SBI Cards and Payment Services Ltd. will be removed from the MSCI India Index. Astral and Balkrishna Industries will, however, be moved to the MSCI India Smallcap Index.

items.title: Stocks to buy in 2026 for long term: Siemens, Zydus Lifesciences among 5 stocks that could give 10-20% return
items.description: Brokerages remain bullish on a host of stocks across pharmaceuticals, infrastructure, financial services and industrials, with several counters offering double-digit upside potential.We have collated a list of recommendations from top brokerage firms from ETNow and other sources:

items.title: Dividend alert! Last day to buy HAL, HPCL, IOC among 40 stocks for dividends. How many do you own?
items.description: Under Sebi’s T+1 settlement cycle, investors need to purchase a company’s shares at least one trading day before the record date to ensure the shares are credited to their demat accounts in time, and they become eligible for the corporate action. Accordingly, today is the last opportunity for investors to buy the shares so that they are credited to their accounts by the record date (August 14), making them eligible for the dividend.

items.title: Positive Breakout: These 9 stocks cross above their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the Nifty500 pack, nine stocks' closing prices crossed above their 200 DMA (Daily Moving Averages) on August 12, 2026, according to stockedge.com's technical scan data. Traders use the 200-day daily moving average (DMA) as a key indicator to determine the overall trend in a particular stock. As long as the stock is priced above the 200-day SMA on the daily timeframe, it is generally considered to be in an overall uptrend. Take a look:

items.title: Groww leads India's top brokerages in July with over 70,000 new active accounts
items.description: Groww strengthened its brokerage lead in July, adding over seventy thousand active accounts.  This growth contrasts with a general industry slowdown in user additions this year.  Zerodha, the second-largest broker, continued to lose active accounts, shrinking its user base.  Angel One and Upstox Securities also experienced declines in their active client numbers.  HDFC Securities similarly shed active accounts during the month and year.

items.title: Godrej Consumer shares tumble on CEO exit, technicals signal more downside
items.description: Godrej Consumer Products shares have experienced a notable drop following the unexpected exit of the chief executive. This abrupt change has raised significant concerns among investors about the future leadership in a volatile market environment. Aasif Malbari has been appointed as the new managing director and chief executive to steer the company.

items.title: Sebi sees no CAS manipulation, eyes more participation
items.description: In a recent statement, Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey confirmed that the closing auction sessions showed no manipulation. He linked earlier discrepancies to cautious trading in the newly implemented system. Notably, mutual funds have significantly increased activity in these sessions. Additionally, Sebi is looking into strategies to bolster both participation and liquidity in commodity derivatives, while also striving to ease access for institutional investors within Indian markets.

items.title: Federal Bank, IDFC First Bank surge in credit card growth, challenging HDFC Bank
items.description: Recent data reveals that Federal Bank and IDFC First Bank have collectively issued over twenty-two lakh new credit cards, almost paralleling HDFC Bank's own expansions. Together, they represent twenty-one percent of the newly released cards, suggesting a noticeable change in the competitive dynamics of the credit card sector as the dominance of the top four issuers appears to be waning.

items.title: Stocks in news: UltraTech Cement, Tata Motors PV, Axis Bank, Apollo Hospitals and Ircon
items.description: Indian equity markets saw a decline on Wednesday, influenced by Middle East tensions and rising oil prices. Several companies will be in focus today due to corporate developments and first-quarter earnings reports. UltraTech Cement shares are set for a block deal, while Apollo Hospitals reported strong profit growth. Lenskart Solutions and Astral also announced significant profit increases for the first quarter.

items.title: D-St set for a negative opening as GIFT Nifty signals weak start
items.description: Indian stock indices closed in the red on August 12, reflecting growing unease in the market. The Nifty 50 lost 35.75 points, closing at 24,435.95. The increase in crude oil costs dampened investor confidence, prompting foreign portfolio investors to offload shares worth Rs 1,002.50 crore. Meanwhile, the Indian rupee remained under pressure, trading around 95.32 against the dollar.

items.title: Southern banks on a golden lending streak; gold-loan books swell 2x
items.description: South Indian banks have seen their gold-loan portfolios nearly double in three years.  This significant growth is driven by rising gold prices and increased demand for credit.  Federal Bank, CSB Bank, and others experienced substantial portfolio expansions.  CSB Bank recorded the fastest growth, more than doubling its gold loan book.  Gold loans now represent a significant portion of advances for these regional lenders.

items.title: Banks to reveal loan rates every month in RBI's disclosure tweak
items.description: The Reserve Bank of India has proposed new lending rate guidelines. Regulated entities must declare lending rates monthly and reset floating loans quarterly. Total charges for microfinance and small loans will be capped by the regulator. These new norms aim to harmonize interest rate determination methods. Final guidelines will take effect from April 1, 2027.

items.title: Tata Motors shares jump 6% after strong Q1; Nomura upgrades stock, CLSA retains Outperform rating
items.description: Tata Motors shares jumped after Q1 FY27 net profit surged 83% YoY to Rs 2,560 crore, aided by mark-to-market gains on Tata Capital investments. Revenue rose 19% YoY to Rs 20,667 crore.

items.title: Buy, Sell or Hold: Citi remains neutral on Lenskart; Nomura upgrades Tata Motors to buy
items.description: Brokerages remain positive on select stocks, with Nomura upgrading Tata Motors’ commercial vehicle business to Buy and Citi retaining a Neutral call on Lenskart despite a higher target price. Motilal Oswal also maintains a Buy rating on Hindustan Aeronautics, citing strong growth and execution prospects, while valuations remain a key consideration.

items.title: Reliance Industries, Adani Enterprises among 10 stocks with highest DII buying up to Rs 22,600 crore in Q1
items.description: Domestic institutional investors stepped up buying in several stocks during the June quarter, with DII holdings rising sharply across a number of companies. The increase in ownership came alongside varied stock price performances, highlighting the stocks where domestic institutions raised their exposure the most during the quarter. Here’s the full list.

items.title: Will largecaps outshine smallcaps on Dalal Street? Here’s what analysts say
items.description: As investors navigate Dalal Street, there’s a growing sentiment that large-cap stocks might soon reclaim leadership. Despite slight gains in the Nifty 50 index, small-cap segments have showcased remarkable dynamism. Recent mutual fund data indicates an ongoing fascination with high-risk small and mid-cap schemes. Interestingly, large-cap funds faced their first monthly outflow in two and a half years.

items.title: Lenskart Solutions shares jump 7% after Q1 results; Jefferies, Goldman Sachs, 3 others raise target price
items.description: Lenskart shares rose after Q1 FY27 profit surged 182% YoY to Rs 228 crore, while revenue grew 34% and EBITDA jumped 61%. Margins also improved sharply, with product margin crossing 70%. Jefferies, Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs remain positive, citing strong growth, margin expansion and premiumisation, with target prices implying up to 22% upside.

items.title: Jio Financial shares jump 3% as Bank of America set to acquire 50% stake in Jio Credit for Rs 18,268 crore
items.description: Jio Financial Services shares: Bank of America agreed to acquire up to 49.9% in its lending arm Jio Credit through a Rs 18,268 crore joint venture deal. The US bank will initially take 26.5%, with the stake potentially rising to 49.9% via warrants, subject to approvals. Jio Credit had an AUM of Rs 30,667 crore as of June 2026.

items.title: Sensex falls over 200 points, Nifty below 24,350 as expiry volatility looms. What lies ahead?
items.description: Indian equities extended losses on Thursday, with Sensex falling over 150 points and Nifty declining over 95 points amid expiry-day volatility. Bajaj Finance and IndiGo led gains, while M&M and Kotak Mahindra Bank slipped. Broader markets remained mixed, with auto and financial stocks gaining, while IT, metal, pharma and FMCG indices declined.

items.title: India said to plan easier rules to boost micro-cap listings
items.description: Sebi is considering sweeping SME IPO reforms to broaden eligibility, boost investor participation and reduce listing costs. Proposed changes include allowing companies valued up to Rs 4,000 crore to list on SME platforms, removing minimum trade sizes, and easing market-making and underwriting requirements. The regulator is expected to issue a consultation paper seeking public comments.

items.title: HAL shares gain 2% after Q1 earnings beat estimates. Nomura, other brokerages hike target price
items.description: In the first quarter of FY27, Hindustan Aeronautics showcased a robust 15% rise in net profit, prompting brokerages to adjust their target prices for HAL shares. Notably, Nomura retained its buy rating while upping its target to Rs 6,314. Meanwhile, Motilal Oswal also revised its target to Rs 5,800, attributing this to the impressive quarterly results. The company anticipates ramping up Tejas deliveries starting FY28.

items.title: F&O Radar: Call Ratio Spread strategy for SBI shares this week
items.description: State Bank of India has delivered a sideways range breakout supported by solid volumes, holding strong above key EMAs. Choice Broking recommends a Call Ratio Spread derivative strategy for August expiry, targeting upside levels of Rs 1,100-1,125 with a favourable risk-reward ratio of 1:2.51.

items.title: Godrej Consumer among 4 F&O stocks with sharp rise in futures open interest
items.description: As of August 12, four stocks in the NSE F&O pack recorded a sharp rise in futures open interest, with open interest increasing by more than 10% compared with the previous trading session. Futures open interest represents the number of active, unexpired futures contracts in a particular security. A rise in open interest indicates that market participants are either initiating new positions or increasing their existing positions in the futures market.

items.title: Nalco among 5 stocks flashing bullish signals, hinting at a possible uptrend
items.description: On August 12, nine stocks in the Nifty500 appeared on the ‘White Marubozu’ bullish scanner, according to StockEdge’s technical scan data. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis that occurs when the opening price is the lowest for a given period and the closing price is the highest.Represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and a small or nonexistent lower shadow, it indicates strong buying pressure throughout the session. Traders interpret it as a signal that buyers were in control from the opening to the closing, often using such patterns for informed decisions about future price movements in financial markets.

items.title: Bharat Heavy Electricals among 5 stocks showing bullish RSI upswing
items.description: On August 12, five Nifty500 stocks that gained over 3.5% were highlighted in the RSI Trending Up scan, based on data from StockEdge.com. An uptrend signal is generated when the RSI value crosses above 50 from below. "RSI trending up" means that the Relative Strength Index (RSI) values are increasing, suggesting strengthening momentum in the stock's price. This can indicate potential upward movement and may be used by traders to identify buying opportunities.

items.title: Chandra’s Rs 25 lakh crore Tata legacy: Revenue up 71%, PAT 3.6x and a 19x multibagger
items.description: N Chandrasekaran has significantly boosted Tata's legacy, achieving a remarkable increase in market capitalization totaling Rs 25 lakh crore. Under his leadership, the group's aggregate revenue soared by seventy-one percent, and profit after tax showed impressive growth. Titan and Trent stood out as key wealth creators, while various Tata firms also enjoyed substantial market gains. However, with a leadership transition on the horizon, the group must navigate ongoing business challenges.

items.title: Will Bharti Airtel’s ARPU increase after scrapping Rs 299, other popular prepaid plans? What JM Financial says
items.description: Bharti Airtel could see a 2% rise in ARPU after withdrawing four entry-level prepaid plans, including the popular Rs 299 pack, JM Financial said. Subscribers will now need to opt for the Rs 349 plan, a roughly 16% price hike, while Rs 199 and Rs 219 plans remain unchanged.

items.title: Astral shares rally 10% following Q1 results; Citi sees target price at Rs 1,900, Nuvama upgrades stock to 'Buy'
items.description: Astral shares surged nearly 10% after strong Q1 FY27 results, with profit rising 51.8% YoY. Citi retained a Buy rating with a Rs 1,900 target, while UBS maintained Accumulate. Nuvama upgraded the stock to Buy, citing strong pipe volumes and margin prospects, while Motilal Oswal retained Buy and CLSA maintained Hold.

items.title: Paytm management gets Sebi show cause notice over timing of 2023 loan disclosure announcement
items.description: Paytm management has received a Sebi show-cause notice over the timing and classification of information disclosed in a December 2023 corporate announcement. The company said its key managerial personnel are evaluating the notice and will respond within 14 days. The development comes after Paytm reported strong Q1 FY27 earnings and Bernstein raised its target.

items.title: Which Tata stocks look attractive now? Jefferies picks 4; flags TCS and 2 others
items.description: Jefferies believes Tata group stocks should remain driven by business fundamentals despite N Chandrasekaran’s planned exit as Tata Sons chairman in February 2027. The brokerage’s top picks are Tata Consumer Products, Tata Steel, Indian Hotels and Voltas.

items.title: Q1 earnings show resilience as demand, cost headwinds prove less severe than expected: ICRA
items.description: ICRA said India Inc’s Q1 FY27 earnings began on a stronger-than-expected note, with revenue growth accelerating to 22%. Despite margin pressure from higher commodity costs and weakness in oil refining and IT services, consumption-led sectors remained resilient. Healthy corporate balance sheets, rising capex and improving credit metrics offer support.

items.title: Thyrocare shares crack 8% as promoter Docon Technologies sells 10% stake
items.description: Thyrocare Technologies shares fell after promoter Docon Technologies sold around 1.58 crore shares, cutting its stake from 60.92% to 51.02%. Docon remains the diagnostics company’s promoter and holding company.

items.title: 8 midcap stocks surged up to 125% in a year; 4 became multibaggers. Do you own any?
items.description: At first glance, the market seems to have gone nowhere over the last year. The Nifty 50 remained almost flat, slipping just 0.21%. But beneath that quiet surface, a very different story was unfolding in the midcap space. The Nifty Midcap 150 delivered a solid 12% gain.The real excitement was within the midcap index. Around 18 midcap stocks surged more than 50%, with eight of them delivering gains of 80–125%. Even more striking, four of these stocks more than doubled in value, significantly multiplying investors’ wealth in just a year. So, while the headline index appeared relatively subdued, pockets of the midcap universe were quietly creating exceptional wealth. Sometimes, the biggest market stories aren’t visible in the index, they’re hidden beneath it. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: Munjal Auto Industries shares soar 15%, hit 52-week high after Q1 results. What moved the stock?
items.description: Munjal Auto Industries reported a strong Q1 FY27 performance, with consolidated revenue rising sharply and the company turning profitable from a year-ago loss. Both its auto components and composite products segments recorded healthy growth, while a mark-to-market gain on mutual fund investments also supported other income.

items.title: Sugar stocks Balrampur Chini, Dhampur Sugar, Dalmia Bharat Sugar, others rally up to 7%. Here’s why
items.description: Sugar stocks rose sharply on Thursday as domestic sugar prices climbed 8-10% in a month to a seven-year high. Rising global sugar prices, worsening supply prospects in Brazil, higher ethanol blending, weather risks and lower output estimates in Thailand and India are tightening global supplies and supporting sugar prices.

items.title: UBS upgrades MCX rating to Buy with Rs 3,800 target price: Can it boost the stock?
items.description: UBS upgraded MCX to Buy from Neutral and raised its target price to Rs 3,800, citing attractive valuations, resilient trading volumes and positive regulatory developments. The brokerage also raised its FY27-FY29 EPS estimates by 4%-9%, while expecting strong commodity volatility and operating leverage to support earnings growth.

items.title: KRN Heat Exchanger shares hit 5% upper circuit as Q1 net profit more than doubles
items.description: Shares of KRN Heat Exchanger and Refrigeration hit a upper circuit on Thursday, following a strong Q1 FY27 earnings performance. The rally was driven by robust demand across both domestic and international markets.

items.title: Lenskart’s Meller sunglasses are Ray-Ban of the future, says Jefferies. Here’s why Wall Street giant is bullish
items.description: Lenskart’s strong Q1 FY27 performance, marked by sharp profit growth, revenue expansion and improving margins, has strengthened the bullish case among brokerages. Jefferies sees further potential from international growth, premiumisation, store expansion and Meller, which it believes could become a major global brand.

items.title: Medium-term investing: You cannot remove the risk; try to get the odds in your favour. 5 large-caps with upside potential of up to 25%
items.description: The mood has improved, but it is too early to give the all-clear. There is still an element of uncertainty in the market. At a time like this, the answer is not to stay out of the market, and it is not to jump in with both feet either. It is to invest carefully; in the kind of companies that can handle whatever the next few months can bring.

items.title: Solar Industries shares jump 8% to fresh lifetime high after Q1 net profit soars 93% YoY to Rs 653 crore
items.description: Solar Industries shares surged over 8% after the company reported a 93% YoY rise in Q1 FY27 net profit to Rs 652.55 crore and 70% revenue growth. Strong defence, domestic and international explosives businesses, a Rs 21,350 crore order book and Rs 14,000 crore FY27 revenue guidance boosted investor confidence in growth prospects.

items.title: Earnings growth to play larger role in determining portfolio returns than valuation re-rating: Nilesh Shah
items.description: Earnings growth is likely to play a larger role in determining portfolio returns than valuation re-rating in the near term, as valuations of Indian equities remain neither cheap nor expensive, according to Nilesh Shah, Managing Director, Kotak Mahindra Asset Management Company.

items.title: Sebi mulls Rs 5 cr securities asset route for accredited investor status for individuals
items.description: Sebi has proposed an initiative to include securities-market assets as a criterion for accredited investor status. Individuals holding five crore rupees in these assets will be eligible, thereby expanding the investor base for alternative investment funds. The regulator anticipates that approximately 3.7 lakh individuals will meet the revised standards, with investment managers playing a key role in confirming accredited status during the onboarding process.

items.title: Lenskart Solutions among 7 stocks hitting 52-week highs; surge up to 20% in a month
items.description: On Thursday, the benchmark Sensex advanced 113 points to close at 78,079. Amid this positive market movement, seven stocks from the BSE 200 index touched fresh 52-week highs, marking their strongest price levels in the past year. A 52-week high is generally considered a positive technical indicator, reflecting strong investor interest, improving market sentiment, and the potential for further upward momentum.

items.title: Two Trades for Today: A top realty firm for a rise of 5.4%, a mid-cap IT stock for a gain of almost 7.5%
items.description: Our technical analysts identify select stocks every trading day that may gain momentum even in volatile markets. Here are the technical calls for today.

items.title: Sebi proposes asset threshold for individuals, corporates to widen accredited investor pool
items.description: Sebi is set to broaden the criteria for accredited investors, allowing individuals boasting securities assets of Rs 5 crore to qualify for participation. Additionally, body corporates with assets totaling Rs 20 crore will also be considered eligible. This strategic move is designed to encourage greater engagement in alternative investment funds. Interested parties are invited to submit their public comments by September 3.

items.title: Weekly Top Picks: These stocks scored 10 on 10 on Stock Reports Plus
items.description: Stock Reports Plus, powered by Refinitiv, undertakes detailed company analysis for 4,000+ listed stocks. In addition to detailed company analyses, the report also collates analysts’ forecasts and trend analysis for each component. An average score in Stock Reports Plus is calculated by undertaking quantitative analysis of five key investment tools – earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum.
